seo.title: IRATA Level 2 — Lead Rope Access Technician | RAC
seo.description: Step up from operator to rigger. Focused on rigging, complex rescues, and taking responsibility for a teammate’s safety.

course.summary: Step up from operator to rigger. Focused on rigging, complex rescues, and taking responsibility for a teammate’s safety.
prerequisites: Hold a valid IRATA Level 1 certificate
Minimum 1,000 logged working hours and at least 12 months since Level 1 certification
A complete IRATA logbook countersigned by a Level 3
outcomes: Rig and prove simple to intermediate anchor systems
Build mechanical advantage hauling systems to raise and lower loads
Perform rescues from re-anchors, deviations, and traverse lines
Assess rigging risk and communicate it clearly to the team
Support a Level 3 in supervising a worksite

syllabus.title: Day 1 — Review & Rigging Theory
syllabus.detail: Level 1 manoeuvre refresh, load theory, anchor angles, safety factors, and selecting structural anchor points.

syllabus.title: Day 2 — Anchor Systems
syllabus.detail: Y-hangs, re-anchors, large deviations, horizontal and vertical aid climbing, and proof-loading systems.

syllabus.title: Day 3 — Hauling & Lowering
syllabus.detail: 3:1 and 5:1 systems, progress capture, load transfer, and lifting with tripods or davit arms.

syllabus.title: Day 4 — Complex Rescue
syllabus.detail: Rescues past re-anchors and deviations, rescues from traverse lines, and stretcher handling.

syllabus.title: Day 5 — Consolidation
syllabus.detail: Time-pressured integrated scenarios, rescue plan documentation, and an internal mock assessment.

syllabus.title: Day 6 — IRATA Assessment
syllabus.detail: Independent assessment covering rigging, manoeuvres, complex rescue, and written theory.

course.certificate: IRATA Level 2 card and certificate, valid for 3 years, registered in the IRATA International database.

sections.body:
## The biggest step in a rope access career

What separates Level 1 from Level 2 is not the number of manoeuvres — it is responsibility. At Level 2 you rig systems that will hold someone else, and you must be able to explain why those systems are sound.

## Before you arrive

Make sure your logbook is complete and countersigned before day one — the IRATA Assessor will inspect it, and an inadequate logbook will disqualify you from assessment. Our team will review your logbook in advance at no charge.

sections.title: Secure your seat on the next cohort
sections.text: Send your name, the number of participants, and the month you are aiming for. We confirm seat availability and paperwork the same working day.
